questions.question: Let A1A2 . . . A12 be a regular dodecagon. questions.question: From B and E, altitudes BF and EG are drawn onto side AC. Compute CF CG− AF AG.
questions.solution: Answer: 2. From B and E, altitudes BF and EG are drawn onto side AC. Compute CF CG− AF AG. Geometry Test Solutions April 8, 2023 Answer: 2 Solution: Let ∠BAC = 3a and AB = x. Observe first that, by the angle bisector theorem, AD AC = DE EC , so AD = AC· DE EC = 5· 3 5 = 3. Then, △ADC is a 3-4-5 triangle, so ∠ADC = 90◦. Since AD bisects ∠BAE and is perpendicular to BE, we have that △BAE is isosceles, which gives us BD = 3 2 and AE =AB =x. Now we know that BF = x sin(3a), AF = x cos(3a), EG = x sin(a), and AG = x cos(a). Since BF is parallel to EG, CF CG = BF EG = x sin(3a) x sin(a) = 3− 4 sin2a, using the triple angle formula. Similarly, AF AG = x cos(3a) x cos(a) = 4 cos2a− 3. Then CF CG− AF AG = 3− 4 sin2a− 4 cos2a + 3 = 6− 4 = 2 .

questions.question: In triangle ABC with AB = 10, let D be a point on side BC such that AD bisects ∠BAC. If CD BD = 2 and the area of ABC is 50, compute the value of ∠BAD in degrees.
questions.solution: Answer: 15◦. In triangle ABC with AB = 10, let D be a point on side BC such that AD bisects ∠BAC. If CD BD = 2 and the area of ABC is 50, compute the value of ∠BAD in degrees. Answer: 15◦ Solution: Since AD bisects ∠BAC, we have by the Angle-Bisector Theorem that AB BD = AC CD =⇒ AC = CD BD·AB = 20. Let E be the point on AC such that BE⊥AC. Since the area of ∆ABC is 50, we have AC·BE 2 = 50 =⇒ BE = 5. But ∆ABE is a right triangle and AB = 2BE, so ∆ABE must be a 30-60-90 triangle. It follows that ∠BAC = 30◦ so ∠BAD = 15◦ .

questions.question: Let ABCD be a quadrilateral such that AB = BC = 13, CD = DA = 15 and AC = 24. Let the midpoint of AC be E. What is the area of the quadrilateral formed by connecting the incenters of ABE, BCE , CDE , and DAE?
questions.solution: Answer: 25. Let ABCD be a quadrilateral such thatAB =BC = 13,CD =DA = 15 andAC = 24. Let the midpoint of AC be E. What is the area of the quadrilateral formed by connecting the incenters of ABE, BCE , CDE , and DAE? Answer: 25 Solution: SinceE is the midpoint ofAC,AE =CE = 12. Also, from AB =BC andCD =DA, we see that ABCD is a kite and AC⊥BD. By the Pythagorean Theorem on the four right triangles, we ﬁnd that AE = 5 and DE = 9. LetW ,X,Y , andZ be the incenters of∆ABE,∆BCE ,∆CDE and∆DAE respectively. Note thatWX||AC andYZ||AC and by symmetry,WZ =XY , so WXYZ is an isosceles trapezoid. The semiperimeter of ∆ABE is 5+12+13 2 = 15, so the inradius is 15 − 13 = 2. Similarly, we can compute that the inradius of ∆CDE is 9+12+15 2 − 15 = 3. It follows that WX = 2(2) = 4 and YZ = 2(3) = 6. Drawing perpendiculars from W to AC and Z to AC, we see that these perpdiculars are exactly the inradii of ∆ABE and∆DAE respectively, so the height of the trapezoid is 2 + 3 = 5. Thus, the area of WXYZ is 10(5) 2 = 25 .

questions.question: In ∆ABC, ∠ABC = 75 ◦ and ∠BAC is obtuse. Points D and E are on AC and BC, respectively, such that AB BC = DE EC and ∠DEC = ∠EDC . Compute ∠DEC in degrees.
questions.solution: Answer: 85. In ∆ABC, ∠ABC = 75◦ and ∠BAC is obtuse. Points D and E are on AC and BC, respectively, such that AB BC = DE EC and ∠DEC = ∠EDC . Compute ∠DEC in degrees. Answer: 85 Solution: Extend AC past A, and draw F on AC such that AB = FB . Note that AB BC = F B BC = DE EC , and since ∠FBC = ∠DEC we have∆FBC ∼∆DEC . Next, we perform some angle chasing. Let ∠DEC = ∠EDC = x. By similar triangles, we have ∠FBC = ∠BFC =x as well. Furthermore, FB =AB, so∆FAB is isoceles, and thus ∠FAB =x as well. Now ∠ABC = 75◦, so we compute ∠FBA = ∠FBC− ∠ABC =x− 75. The angles of a triangle sum to 180 ◦, giving us the equation 3x− 75 = 180, which solves to x = 85 .

questions.question: Let E be an ellipse with major axis length 4 and minor axis length 2. Inscribe an equilateral triangle ABC in E such that A lies on the minor axis and BC is parallel to the major axis. Compute the area of ∆ABC.
questions.solution: Answer: 192. Let E be an ellipse with major axis length 4 and minor axis length 2. Inscribe an equilateral triangle ABC in E such that A lies on the minor axis and BC is parallel to the major axis. Compute the area of ∆ABC. Answer: 192 √ 3 169 Solution: Consider a transformation that scales along the major axis by a factor of 1 2 so that the ellipse becomes a circle of radius 1 and the equilateral triangle becomes an isoceles triangle. Let the transformed triangle be denoted AB′C′. Now, let x = |B′C′| 2 . Then the original length |BC| = 4x and since ∆ABC is equilateral, |AB| =|BC| = 4x. Next, we calculate the altitude dropped from A′ as 1 + √ 1−x2. Applying Pythagoras’s theorem, we get that |AB|2 = (1 + √ 1−x2)2 + 4x2. Substitute |AB| = 4x in and solving for x2, we get that x2 = 48 169. Finally, we calculate the area of ∆ABC. Since ∆ABC is equilateral, its area is given by √ 3 4|BC|2 = √ 3 4 16x2. Substituting in x2 = 48 169 and simplifying, we obtain 192 √ 3 169 .

questions.question: In cyclic quadrilateral ABCD , AB∼= AD. If AC = 6 and AB BD = 3 5, ﬁnd the maximum possible area of ABCD .
questions.solution: Answer: 5. In cyclic quadrilateral ABCD , AB∼=AD. If AC = 6 and AB BD = 3 5, ﬁnd the maximum possible area of ABCD . Answer: 5 √ 11 Solution: We claim that the area of ABCD is constant, though the shape of ABCD depends on the radius of the circumscribing circle. First, by Ptolemy’s, we have AB×CD +BC×AD =AB(BC +CD) =AC×BD =⇒ BC +CD =AC× BD AB = 10. Now, extend CB past B to a point E such that BE∼=CD. Since ABCD is cyclic, ∠ABC and ∠ADC are supplementary, so ∠ADC∼= ∠ABE. Hence, ∆ADC∼=∆ABE, and so ABCD has the same area as ACE. ACE is isosceles with leg 6 and base CE =CB +BE =CB +DC = 10. Hence, the length of the altitude to the base is √ 62− 52 = √ 11, and the area is 5 √ 11 .
